paragraphs: Abba the bloodletter—that is, one who lets blood. A greeting came to him from heaven every day, to Abaye every eve of Shabbat, and to Rava on the eve of Yom Kippur. Rava was distressed in comparison with Abaye, and Abaye in comparison with Abba the bloodletter. They told him, “You cannot act as he does.” Abaye sent a pair of rabbis to test him, and he dealt charitably with them (Ta'anit 21b). Mamre is Abba the bloodletter, who was a physician. “Mamre” has the numerical value of “Raphael.” (It should read “rafa,” meaning a healer; Raphael is the angel whom the Holy One, blessed be He, sent to heal Abraham.) Because he advised Abraham to circumcise himself without fearing the danger, he was therefore a physician (G.N.).
